## Mixed model data

`mixed_model_data` is a named list containing the two visit datasets. The labels `itt` and `pp` let the later loops select a population by name. Each dataset still contains repeated rows per participant; the helper's random intercept accounts for that dependence. `mixed_model_fits`, `mixed_model_tables` and `mixed_model_estimates` begin empty and will hold the fitted models, their coefficient tables and the estimates the plots draw.

```{r}
#| label: mixed-model-data
#| eval: false
```

## Mixed models overall

For each population and outcome, this fits the model once with `fit_mixed_model()`, then makes its coefficient table with `tabulate_model_terms()` and its estimates with `estimate_effects()`. Read the nested brackets as a filing system: population, then outcome, then analysis. For example, `mixed_model_tables[["itt"]][["act_score"]][["overall"]]` selects the overall intention-to-treat ACT table after an authorized run. These are coefficient tables, not a single intervention-effect estimate per visit.

The model and what its coefficients mean are explained in [Longitudinal data and mixed models](methods_longitudinal.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: mixed-models-overall
#| eval: false
```

## Mixed models subgroups

The extra loop asks whether the arm-by-visit pattern differs by one baseline subgroup at a time. Children and adults are compared only for outcomes used in both groups; the adult and caregiver quality-of-life measures are not interchangeable. A missing outcome or model predictor can change the rows used by a particular fit, so the same dataset name does not guarantee the same analysis sample for every outcome.

Reading the three-way visit × arm × subgroup terms is covered in [Interactions](methods_interactions.qmd#reading-the-coefficients-linear-mixed-models), and the meaning of their p-values in [What a p-value for interaction means](methods_interaction_p_values.qmd).
